ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, $AB$ and $AC$ are the sides of an inscribed square and an inscribed equilateral triangle in the circle $\odot O$, respectively, and $BC$ is one side of an inscribed regular $n$-sided polygon in the circle. What is the value of $n$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} As shown in the figure, draw lines AO, BO, and CO.\\
Since AB and AC are respectively one side of a square and an equilateral triangle inscribed in $\odot$O,\\
it follows that $ \angle AOB=\frac{360^\circ}{4}=90^\circ$ and $ \angle AOC=\frac{360^\circ}{3}=120^\circ$,\\
therefore $ \angle BOC=30^\circ$,\\
hence $ n=\frac{360^\circ}{30^\circ}=\boxed{12}$.

ready3_open_rewrite.resolved_answer: \textbf{Solution:} As shown in the figure, draw lines AO, BO, and CO.\\ Since AB and AC are respectively one side of a square and an equilateral triangle inscribed in $\odot$O,\\ it follows that $ \angle AOB=\frac{360^\circ}{4}=90^\circ$ and $ \angle AOC=\frac{360^\circ}{3}=120^\circ$,\\ therefore $ \angle BOC=30^\circ$,\\ hence $ n=\frac{360^\circ}{30^\circ}=\boxed{12}$.

Image description: In the figure there is a circle, with the center labeled O. Point A is at the upper left of the circle, point B is at the lower left of the circle, and point C is at a position below the circle and slightly to the left; all three points are on the circle. Looking along the smaller arc on the left side in the direction from A to C, B is located between A and C. The figure also draws the related chord lines of the inscribed square with AB as a side and the inscribed equilateral triangle with AC as a side.
Reasoning: AB is one side of a square inscribed in the circle, so the central angle or minor arc AB that it subtends is 360° ÷ 4 = 90°. AC is one side of an equilateral triangle inscribed in the circle, so the central angle or minor arc AC that it subtends is 360° ÷ 3 = 120°. From the figure it can be known that minor arc AC is composed of minor arc AB and minor arc BC, therefore minor arc BC = 120° - 90° = 30°. Also because BC is one side of a regular n-gon inscribed in the same circle, the central angle subtended by each side is 360°/n. Thus 360°/n = 30°, solving gives n = 12.
